files.author: Arthur W. Pink
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Union with Christ in Baptism: A Baptismal Sermon
sourceMetadata.description: In this rare sermon from 1927 taken down by shorthand in Australia, Baptist preacher Arthur Pink presents us with a glimpse of our union with Christ, the meaning of Christian baptism, and the glory of the gospel. He exhibits from Scripture the glory of our union with our Savior in our standing before God, our acceptance with the Father, and our entering into and enjoying the inheritance. This is what the symbol of baptism points to. When the sinless Son of God was baptized He was demonstrating in a symbol His union with His people. In our baptism, we show our oneness with Him. The "momentary burial" of the one being baptized followed by their rising again from the water is a beautiful picture of Christ's work for us, Christ's work in us, and Christ's work through us in the Christian life of sanctification to follow.

files.title: A Husband's Love
files.author: Chapel Library contributors
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: A Husband's Love
sourceMetadata.description: With love for Christ and a burning desire to help men understand their God-ordained roles as husbands, we offer this issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster, A Husband’s Love. Matthew Henry sets the stage for the rest of the articles with his comments on Genesis 2—man’s responsibility to love his wife began in the Garden of Eden. David Martyn Lloyd-Jones then describes a Christlike love for us, since the Lord Jesus is the model from which husbands must learn how to love. What are the responsibilities of such a love? Ezekiel Hopkins gives us an overview. John Angell James then gives us a detailed survey of how Christ loved His church. In a second article, Lloyd-Jones carefully and biblically explains how men may love their wives as they love themselves. In a profound and deeply challenging article, Benjamin Palmer gives us insight into the force of love, the abuse of authority, and the affect these have on a woman’s heart. This article may be a difficult read for some, but it is worth repeated and prayerful reading. Men know well how to love themselves, and John Angell James appeals to them to apply the same to their wives. And who better than Charles Spurgeon can take the golden example of Christ loving His church and bringing it home to a husband’s heart? He does so with great power, clarity, and verve. Finally, with a heart full of Puritan fire, George Swinnock offers up a husband’s prayer for the grace to love as Christ and for the spiritual wellbeing of his dear wife. These articles will richly repay those who prayerfully apply them.

articles.title: It Began in a Garden
articles.description: God created Adam, placed him in the Garden of Eden, and then fashioned one of his ribs to make him a wife. So, a man’s God-ordained role as husband began in that unique time and place, when God gave the first man the first wife.

articles.title: A Christlike Love
articles.description: What is Christlike love? To understand what God requires of a husband’s love, a man must first have a biblical understanding of Christ’s love for His church.

articles.title: The Responsibilities of Love
articles.description: Husbands owe their wives Christlike love, but how are they to understand and apply this to their marriage?

articles.title: As Christ Loved the Church
articles.description: a detailed survey of the extraordinary ways that Christ loved and loves His people: the doctrine of the cross lies at the heart of a husband’s love.

articles.title: Loving Your Wife as Yourself
articles.description: Many husbands simply do not understand the clear, biblical fact that their wives are a part of them; but what does that mean and how are men to do it?

articles.title: The Force of Love
articles.description: Do men really understand the God-commanded responsibility to love their wives? And why does God have to command men to do so? The answers are profound.

articles.title: As Their Own Bodies
articles.description: an appeal to men to ponder deeply the care they so readily lavish upon themselves and to show the same to the women with whom they have covenanted in marriage.

articles.title: The Master's Example
articles.description: Jesus Christ is the golden example of love to His disciples. What kind of love did He have, and how did He show it to His Bride? He will be faithful to her for eternity.

articles.title: A Husband's Prayer
articles.description: a humble plea to the gracious God of heaven for the grace, wisdom, and strength to love, to provide for, to protect, and to biblically direct a wife.

children.title: El amor del esposo
children.description: Por amor a Cristo y por un ardiente deseo de ayudar a los hombres a entender sus roles ordenados por Dios como esposos, ofrecemos este número del Portavoz de la Gracia: El amor del esposo. Matthew Henry prepara el escenario para el resto de los artículos con sus comentarios sobre Génesis 2 —la responsabilidad del hombre de amar a su esposa comenzó en el huerto del Edén—. David Martyn Lloyd-Jones nos describe entonces, un amor semejante al de Cristo, dado que el Señor Jesús es el modelo del cual los esposos deben aprender cómo amar. ¿Cuáles son las responsabilidades de un amor así? Ezekiel Hopkins nos da una visión general. John Angell James nos ofrece un estudio detallado de cómo Cristo amó a su Iglesia. En un segundo artículo, Lloyd-Jones explica, cuidadosa y bíblicamente, cómo los hombres pueden amar a sus esposas como se aman a sí mismos. En un artículo intenso y profundamente desafiante, Benjamin Palmer nos ofrece una perspectiva de la aspereza en el amor, el abuso de autoridad y el efecto que estos tienen en el corazón de una mujer. Este artículo puede ser de difícil lectura para algunos, pero vale la pena leerlo repetidamente y en oración. Los hombres saben bien cómo amarse a sí mismos y John Angell James los exhorta a aplicar lo mismo a sus esposas. ¿Y quién mejor que Charles Spurgeon, puede tomar el ejemplo de oro de Cristo amando a su Iglesia y llevarlo al corazón del esposo? Él lo hace con gran poder, claridad y entusiasmo. Finalmente, con un corazón ardiendo de pasión puritana, George Swinnock ofrece la oración de un esposo por la gracia de amar como Cristo y por el bienestar espiritual de su querida esposa. Estos artículos recompensarán, ricamente, a quienes los apliquen en oración.

files.title: ABCs of Prophetic Scripture
files.author: George H. Clement
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: ABCs of Prophetic Scripture
sourceMetadata.description: The ABCs of the Prophetic Scriptures compares the teachings of  dispensationalism with Scripture. It demonstrates that God has one glorious kingdom, prefigured in Israel, unveiled in the Church, and fulfilled in the eternal age to come. It argues that the Church of Jesus Christ is God’s spiritual Israel; that Christ’s Second Coming will be one event, marking the end of the world; and that the Tribulation, the Millennium, and the Antichrist are all representative of events that have begun to be fulfilled already in the experience of the Church, but may have yet to reach their climax before the return of Christ.

children.title: El ABC de las Escrituras proféticas
children.description: El ABC de las Escrituras proféticas compara las enseñanzas del dispensacionalismo con las Escrituras. Demuestra que Dios tiene un reino glorioso, prefigurado en Israel, revelado en la iglesia y cumplido en la edad eterna por venir. Argumenta que la iglesia de Jesucristo es el Israel espiritual de Dios; que la segunda venida de Cristo será un evento que marcará el fin del mundo; y que la Tribulación, el Milenio y el Anticristo son todos representativos de eventos que ya han comenzado a cumplirse en la experiencia de la iglesia, pero que aún pueden tener que alcanzar su clímax antes del regreso de Cristo.

files.author: Chapel Library contributors
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Abortion
sourceMetadata.description: This issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster focuses on abortion, a burning ethical issue of our day. Puritan Ezekiel Hopkins helps us understand that abortion is a violation of God's command, "Thou shalt not kill." Presbyterian Peter Barnes gives a snapshot of the terrible scourge of abortion as it is practiced in our day. R.C. Sproul explains why abortion is such a violation of the biblical perspective on human nature as image-bearers of God. George Grant explores the cultural ramifications of parents so given to death. Joel Beeke addresses common arguments used by abortion supporters. R.C. Sproul tackles one of the most common arguments for abortion: an unborn child is not an actual human being. Joel Beeke reproves abortion with the proclamations from God's Word. Franklin Ed Payne demonstrates the soul-chilling connection between the child-sacrificing idolatry of Canaan with the modern holocaust of abortion. Finally, Charles Spurgeon offers hope for the worst of sinners through the gospel of Jesus Christ.

articles.title: Answers to Abortion Arguments
articles.description: Are the arguments for abortion on demand legitimate? These wise, scientific, and biblical answers say no.

articles.title: Great Forgiveness for Great Sin
articles.description: a stirring gospel message of free, immediate, and complete forgiveness to the greatest of sinners.

articles.title: Mankind and the Death Factor
articles.description: a brief history of child killing and the biblical reasons why human societies become cultures of death.

articles.title: Molech Is Alive and Well
articles.description: a penetrating look at the similarities between abortion and child sacrifice with a view of God’s judgment upon both.

articles.title: Proclamations of God's Word
articles.description: six biblical proclamations regarding the killing of unborn human life.

articles.title: The Bible and Sanctity of Life
articles.description: an important discussion revealing that human life is sacred because it is rooted in creation.

articles.title: The Silent Holocaust
articles.description: an overview of the holocaust of abortion, some of the dreadful methods it employs, and an examination of what the Bible says about it.

articles.title: Thou Shalt Not Kill
articles.description: an introduction to the Sixth Commandment, revealing our consequent responsibilities to preserve life.

articles.title: When Does Life Begin?
articles.description: The question of when life begins is connected to the secret of life itself, and the Holy Scriptures clearly indicate that unborn babies are living human beings before they are born.

children.title: Aborto
children.description: Esta edición del Portavoz de la Gracia se centra en el aborto, una cuestión ética candente de nuestros días. El puritano Ezekiel Hopkins nos ayuda a comprender que el aborto constituye una violación del mandamiento de Dios: «No matarás». El presbiteriano Peter Barnes ofrece una panorámica del terrible flagelo del aborto tal como se practica en la actualidad. R.C. Sproul explica por qué el aborto representa una violación tan flagrante de la perspectiva bíblica sobre la naturaleza humana, entendida como portadora de la imagen de Dios. George Grant explora las ramificaciones culturales de unos padres tan entregados a la muerte. Joel Beeke aborda los argumentos habituales esgrimidos por los defensores del aborto. R.C. Sproul refuta uno de los argumentos más comunes a favor del aborto: que el niño no nacido no es un ser humano real. Joel Beeke condena el aborto basándose en las proclamaciones de la Palabra de Dios. Franklin Ed Payne pone de manifiesto la escalofriante conexión existente entre la idolatría cananea —que implicaba el sacrificio de niños— y el holocausto moderno del aborto. Por último, Charles Spurgeon ofrece esperanza para los peores de los pecadores a través del evangelio de Jesucristo.

sourceMetadata.title: Adoniram Judson and the Missionary Call
sourceMetadata.description: Adoniram Judson (1788-1850) was the first missionary to sail abroad from America in the great mission awakening that developed in the early 19th century. Three principal purposes are designed in this presentation of Judson’s life and doctrine. First, there is inspiration for every reader, as Judson exemplifies Christian faith, love, self-discipline, enterprise, perseverance, and godliness. Second, Adoniram Judson set an example of total commitment to inspire missionaries in enduring the inevitable strains peculiar to their calling. Third, there is the reality of the unfinished task of reaching the yet unreached people groups of the world. May Judson’s example contribute to thrusting out many new labourers into the harvest fields.

sourceMetadata.title: Adoption
sourceMetadata.description: Adoption is one of the blessings that God has given us in Christ Jesus. "It is taking a stranger into the relationship of a son and heir." In adoption, God does the following three things: (1) He gives us His name; (2) He sanctifies us by His Spirit; and (3) the Holy Spirit prompts us to cry, "Abba, Father" (Gal 4:6). Adoption is a high honor and is a wonderful demonstration of the love of God to us.

sourceMetadata.title: Advice for Seekers
sourceMetadata.description: Spurgeon speaks to souls who are honestly seeking to know Christ, showing the futility of seeking salvation based on one’s own good works. He shows that Christ is the bridge between God and man, performing the offices of Mediator, Priest, and Savior. Christ is not at fault if the seeker is faithless. He has removed all obstacles, but the seeker must reach out and touch Christ by faith. He must not trust in his own works, but in Christ's finished work. Spurgeon’s illustrations show that God's infinite mercy is sufficient for all who will believe. “The just shall live by faith.”

sourceMetadata.title: Ages to Come, The
sourceMetadata.description: Death and eternity are near every minute, therefore every person must be prepared for life beyond death. We must knowing Him who is “Life Eternal.” Bonar gives examples of the consolation and shelter found in Christ by notable saints as they neared death. As Sin- bearer, Jesus suffered, died, and rose again that He might “bring us to God”. As Sorrow-bearer, Jesus bids those who love Him to “lean hard” on Him, that He may be their comfort and strength. Knowing we will be like Him in eternity, “what manner of persons ought [we] to be” here on earth?

children.title: Los siglos venideros
children.description: La muerte y la eternidad están cerca en todo momento; por tanto, cada persona debe estar preparada para la vida más allá de la muerte. Debemos conocer a Aquel que es la «Vida Eterna». Bonar presenta ejemplos del consuelo y el refugio que santos notables hallaron en Cristo al acercarse a la muerte. Como Aquel que cargó con el pecado, Jesús sufrió, murió y resucitó para «llevarnos a Dios». Como Aquel que carga con el dolor, Jesús invita a quienes le aman a «apoyarse firmemente» en Él, para que sea su consuelo y su fortaleza. Sabiendo que seremos como Él en la eternidad, ¿qué clase de personas debemos ser aquí en la tierra?

sourceMetadata.title: Alive or Dead?
sourceMetadata.description:
J.C. Ryle’s Alive or Dead asks the question faced by every human who has ever lived: Are you among the living or the dead? In his direct and engaging style, Ryle challenges the reader to consider his own condition, and call upon God to turn him in the right direction before he “lays down this booklet.” Sections include
1. All are spiritually dead 
2. All need to be made alive
3. How a dead soul is made alive
4. Are you alive?

children.title: ¿Vivo o muerto?
children.description:
¿Vivo o muerto? por J. C. Ryle, postula la pregunta que ha enfrentado cada ser humano que jamás ha vivido: ¿Te encuentras tú entre los vivos o  los muertos? En su estilo directo y llamativo, el autor desafía al lector a considerar su propia condición antes de “cerrar este librito”. Los temas que trata son: 1. Todos están espiritualmente muertos, 2. Todos necesitan que Dios les dé vida, 3. Cómo cobra vida un alma muerta y 4. ¿Estás vivo?

sourceMetadata.title: All of Grace
sourceMetadata.description: About All of Grace: “The object of this book is the salvation of the reader. He who spoke and wrote it will be greatly disappointed if it does not lead many to the Lord Jesus. It is sent forth in childlike dependence upon the power of God the Holy Ghost, to use it in the conversion of millions, if so He pleases…Reader, do you mean business in reading these pages? If so, we are agreed at the outset; but nothing short of your finding Christ and heaven is the business aimed at here. Oh that we may seek this together! I do so by dedicating this little book with prayer. Will not you join me by looking up to God, and asking him to bless you while you read?”—C.H. Spurgeon, from Chapter One.

children.title: Totalmente por gracia
children.description: Acerca de Toda la Gracia: “El objetivo de este libro es la salvación del lector. El que lo habló y lo escribió se sentirá enormemente decepcionado si no lleva a muchos al Señor Jesús. Este libro se presenta en dependencia similar a la de un niño del poder de Dios el Espíritu Santo, para usarlo en la conversión de millones, si así El lo desea ... Lector, ¿te interesa la lectura de estas páginas? Si es así, estamos de acuerdo desde el principio; pero nada menos que tu búsqueda de Cristo y el cielo es la meta que se dirige aquí. ¡Oh, que podamos buscar esto juntos! Lo hago dedicando este pequeño libro en oración. ¿No te unirás a mí mirando a Dios y pidiéndole que te bendiga mientras lees? ”- C.H. Spurgeon, del Capítulo Uno.

children.title: الكل بالنعمة
children.description: إن غاية هذا الكتاب هي خلاص القاريء . فالشخص الذي كتبه ووعظه سيخيب أمله كثيرا إن لم يقُد كثيرين للرب يسوع المسيح . لقد كتب وأرسل – كاعتماد الأولاد – على قوة الله الروح القدس لكي يستخدمه بتجديد الملايين فلقد كتب وأرسل – كاعتماد الأولاد – على قوة الله الروح القدس لكي يستخدمه بتجديد الملايين فإذا حدث ذلك سيفرح . وبدون شك سيقرأ العديد من النساء والرجال الفقراء هذا الكتاب والله سيزودهم بنعمته . ولكي نصل الى هذه النتيجة فلقد قمت باستخدام لغة بسيطة وتعابير معروفة ولكن إن نظر إليه رجال الفن والعلم فيستطيع الروح القدس أن يؤثر فيهم أيضا لأنه إن كان يُستطاع فهمه من قبل الناس العاديين فكم بالحري أن يكون جذابا للمتعلمين ، ويا ليت البعض يقرؤونه ويصبحون هم أنفسهم رابحي نفوس.

In this excerpt from his book, Matthew Mead shows from Biblical examples just how close one can get to Christ and still not be a Christian. A must read for all who truly want to examine their own faith.

children.title: Presque Chrétien
children.description: Aujourd’hui, beaucoup de ceux qui font profession de foi chrétienne se demandent : « Dans quelle mesure puis-je ressembler à ce monde tout en restant chrétien ? Dans cet extrait tiré d’un de ses livres, Matthew Meade nous montre par des exemples bibliques comment on peut s’approcher de Christ sans pour autant être chrétien. Un incontournable pour tous ceux qui désirent réellement examiner leur foi.

sourceMetadata.title: Am I Really a Christian?
sourceMetadata.description:
Though it would certainly be unkind to give false assurance of salvation to someone who has not been truly converted, it would be equally cruel to withhold comfort and assurance to a weak lamb who suffers with despair over his spiritual state. In his spiritual classic Human Nature in Its Fourfold State, Thomas Boston lists eight "cases" where a true Christian might have spiritual doubts about the authenticity of his faith. Such doubts, Boston notes, "may hinder some persons from the comfortable view of their happy state." Thus, he writes to encourage, comfort, and assure those saints who are burdened with such doubts.

Audio narrated by Dwayne DeSalvo

children.title: ¿Soy realmente un cristiano?
children.description: Publicado originalmente en inglés bajo el título Am I Really a Christian? Este folleto contiene extractos seleccionados de Human Nature in Its Fourfold State, modernizadas para facilitar su comprensión al lector de hoy en día. Jeffrey T. Riddle, pastor de la Iglesia Bautista Reformada de Cristo en Charlottesville, Virginia, proporcionó la abstracción y la modernización.

children.title: Tunay Ba Akong Kristiyano?
children.description: Si Thomas Boston ay naglista ng walong “mga kaso” kung saan ang isang tunay na Kristiyano ay maaaring magkaroon ng espirituwal na pagdududa tungkol sa pagiging tunay ng kanyang pananampalataya. Ang gayong mga pag-aalinlangan, ang sabi ng Boston, “ay maaaring makahadlang sa ilang tao mula sa kumportableng pananaw sa kanilang maligayang kalagayan.” Kaya, sumulat siya upang palakasin ang loob, aliwin, at tiyakin sa mga banal na nabibigatan ng gayong mga pagdududa.

children.title: Ese koko ndi Umukristo?
children.description: Nubwo rwose byaba ari bibi gutanga ibyiringiro byibinyoma by agakiza kumuntu utarahindutse mubyukuri, byaba ari ubugome kimwe kwima ihumure nicyizere kumwana wintama ufite intege nke wihebye kubera umwuka we. Muri kamere ye ya kimuntu yo mu mwuka muri Leta zayo enye, Thomas Boston yanditse "imanza" umunani aho umukristo nyawe ashobora gushidikanya mu mwuka kubyerekeye kwizera kwe. Boston avuga ko gushidikanya, "bishobora kubuza abantu bamwe kubona neza uko bishimye." Rero, yanditse kugirango ashishikarize, ahumurize, kandi yizeze abo bera baremerewe no gushidikanya.

sourceMetadata.title: Andrew Dunn: An Irish Story
sourceMetadata.description: Redemption, forgiveness, and God’s amazing grace is the story of Andrew Dunn.  This small booklet traces the latter part of the life of Andrew Dunn, an “educated Roman Catholic” from Ireland in the mid-18th century.  Although raised a Catholic, Andrew realized his ignorance of the gospel and sought help from his local priest.  Through dialogues with his priest, the reading of the Bible, and the work of the Holy Spirit, Andrew came to understand the truth of Romans 1:16:  “For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ:  for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.”  This booklet is full of the transforming power of God’s gospel and will encourage your walk with Him.

children.title: Andrés Dunn
children.description: Después de 40 años sumido en la ignorancia católica romana, Andrés Dunn consigue acceso a un Nuevo Testamento. Al leer las paginas de este libro Dios le abrió los ojos y entonces pudo ver las falsas doctrinas y practicas que la Iglesia Católica Romana  le había inculcado. No solo esto, sino que Dios le otorgó salvación para su alma a través de la lectura y meditación en este poderoso texto que es la Palabra de Dios ¨Viva y eficaz¨.

files.title: Anguish and Agonies of Spurgeon
files.author: Darrel W. Amundsen
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Anguish and Agonies of Spurgeon
sourceMetadata.description: The sermons of Charles Spurgeon, the beloved preacher, exude great joy in the Lord, and sometimes humor, but he was also no stranger to depression, rejection by others, and physical suffering. His spiritual sufferings taught him to hate sin and cherish God’s holiness. The persecution of those who opposed his ministry was all but crushing, and his many physical ailments were great trials to him.  Through it all he was able to exemplify a confidence in God’s sovereignty and love. In his last sermon he stated that “the heaviest end of the cross lies ever on His shoulders.”  May Charles Spurgeon’s words of trust and reliance help all of God's children when they go through their dark valley.

children.title: சார்லஸ் ஸ்பர்ஜனின் மனவேதனைகளும்பாடுகளும
children.description:
அனைவராலும் நேசிக்கப்பட்ட பிரசங்கியாராகிய சார்லஸ் ஸ்பர்ஜனின் பிரசங்கங்கள் கர்த்தருக்குள் அவர் கொண்டிருந்த மிகுந்த மகிழ்ச்சியை வெளிப்படுத்தின. ஆனால், மனச்சோர்வு, பிறரால் நிராகரிக்கப்படுதல், சரீர வேதனைகள் போன்ற துன்பங்களுக்கும் அவருக்குப் பழக்கமில்லாதவை அல்ல. அவருடைய ஆவிக்குரிய பாடுகள், பாவத்தை வெறுக்கவும் தேவனுடைய பரிசுத்தத்தைப் போற்றவும் அவருக்குக் கற்றுக்கொடுத்தன. அவருடைய ஊழியத்தை எதிர்த்தவர்கள் செய்த துன்புறுத்தல்கள் அவரை முற்றிலும் நசுக்கிப் போடுவதாக அமைந்திருந்தன; மேலும், அவருடைய பலவிதமான சரீர வியாதிகளும் அவருக்கு மாபெரும் சோதனைகளாக இருந்தன.

ஆயினும், இவை எல்லாவற்றின் மத்தியிலும் தேவனுடைய இறையாண்மையிலும் அவருடைய அன்பிலும் அவர் வைத்திருந்த உறுதியான நம்பிக்கையை தமது வாழ்க்கையின் மூலம் எடுத்துக்காட்டினார். தமது கடைசிப் பிரசங்கத்தில் அவர், “சிலுவையின் பாரமான முனை எப்போதும் கிறிஸ்துவின் தோள்களிலேயே இருக்கிறது” என்று கூறினார். கர்த்தரை நம்பியும், அவரையே சார்ந்தும் வாழ்ந்த சார்லஸ் ஸ்பர்ஜனின் இந்த வார்த்தைகள், தேவனுடைய பிள்ளைகள் தங்கள் வாழ்வின் அந்தகாரப் பள்ளத்தாக்குகளைக் கடந்து செல்லும் வேளைகளில் அவர்களுக்கு ஆறுதலையும் நம்பிக்கையையும் அளிப்பதாக இருக்கட்டும்.

sourceMetadata.title: Ann Judson: A Life of Self-denial
sourceMetadata.description: As a young woman, Ann Judson (1789-1826) became the wife of Adoniram Judson, the early leader of American missions. Ann's faith triumphed through years of sorrow, suffering, tragedy, and selfless dedication to the cause of Christ in Burma (Myanmar). Her example to youth of self-denying faithfulness in love for her family and the people of Burma was outstanding, but her biography is not so much the story of a great woman of character but of the amazing grace of a great God!

children.title: Ana Judson: Una vida de abnegación
children.description: Siendo una mujer joven, Ann Judson (1789-1826) se convirtió en la esposa de Adoniram Judson, uno de los primeros líderes de las misiones estadounidenses. La fe de Ann triunfó a través de años de dolor, sufrimiento, tragedia y una dedicación abnegada a la causa de Cristo en Birmania (Myanmar). Su ejemplo para los jovenes —de fidelidad abnegada en el amor hacia su familia y hacia el pueblo de Birmania— fue extraordinario; sin embargo, su biografía no es tanto la historia de una gran mujer de carácter, ¡sino la de la asombrosa gracia de un gran Dios!

files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Anxiety
sourceMetadata.description:
In this short and especially timely tract in view of today’s theatening environment, A. W. Pink urges us to understand that anxiety is a sin “as definitely as theft.” He goes on to point out that this needs to be carefully pondered “so that we don’t excuse it as an innocent infirmity.” He gives three suggestions for overcoming this sin.

  1. Implore the Holy Spirit to grant us a deeper conviction of its enormity.
  2. Make it a subject of earnest prayer that we may be delivered from this evil.
  3. Watch for its beginning, and as soon as we detect an anxious, unbelieving thought, lift up our heart to God and ask for deliverance.

According to Pink, the best antidote for anxiety is frequent meditation on God’s goodness, power, and sufficiency, realizing from Psalm 23 that “The Lord is my Shepherd, I shall not want.”

files.title: Apart
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Apart
sourceMetadata.description: True repentance is always accompanied by sorrow. Even when Christ is seen by faith, and sin is pardoned, the man does not cease to mourn for his sin. Mourning increases as knowledge of guilt grows, and hatred of sin grows as he understands the love of Christ which put away his sin. The prophet Zechariah describes a land full of people mourning for sin. Though the whole land was in mourning, each person mourned for his sin apart from all the others. National sorrow over sin is a sham. Mass repentance is not true repentance. A man who sees his sin must deal with it between himself and God alone. He has no desire to be in the company of others, or to be near to the distractions of the world. Spurgeon urges every soul to get quite alone with God, and repent of his sin, then go forth and try to bring others.

children.title: Apostasía
children.description: Ofrecemos este número de Portavoz de la Gracia para ayudarnos a evaluar nuestro propio estado espiritual. A. W. Pink presenta el tema de la apostasía y la define bíblicamente. Charles Spurgeon nos da muchas razones por las cuales algunos abandonan a Cristo. Ebenezer Erskine nos ayuda a ver la diferencia entre una apostasía parcial y una total. Siempre aparece Hebreos 6:4-6 cuando surge el tema de apostasía. Pink nos da una exposición clara y provechosa de este importante pasaje. En un segundo artículo, Erskine nos enfrenta con lo vil de la apostasía y ofrece aliento para ayudarnos a evitarla. En un sermón realmente penetrante, Samuel Pierce enfoca a los que se apartan de las iglesias de Cristo. Thomas Brooks describe siete características de maestros apóstatas con el fin de ayudarnos a identificarlos y evitarlos. Pueden ser individuos los que se apartan, pero también pueden hacerlo iglesias enteras. Horatius Bonar nos ayuda a reconocer a las iglesias que están haciendo un naufragio de la fe. John Owen pone bien en claro que los pastores juegan un papel vital en ayudar al pueblo de Cristo a evitar la apostasía. Por último, Gardiner Spring nos refresca con la gran provisión de Dios para preservar a sus hijos de la caída final y fatal.

sourceMetadata.description: “Just now we have to do with [those], who are not far from the kingdom, but have come right up to the wicket gate which stands at the head of the way of life. One would think that they would hasten to enter, for a free and open invitation is placed over the entrance, the porter waits to welcome them, and there is but this one way to eternal life. He that is most loaded seems the most likely to pass in and begin the heavenward journey; but what ails the other men? This is what I want to find out. Poor fellows! they have come a long way already to get where they are; and the King’s highway, which they seek, is right before them: why do they not take to the Pilgrim Road at once?…Only the Lord Himself can …lead them to take the great decisive step. Yet the Lord works by means; and I have prepared this little book in the earnest hope that He may work by it to the blessed end of leading seekers to an immediate, simple trust in the Lord Jesus.”          —from the Preface, Charles Spurgeon

children.title: Les attributs de Dieu
children.description:
ATTACHE-TOI DONC À DIEU, ET TU AURAS LA PAIX ; tu jouiras ainsi du bonheur (Job 22.21). Ainsi parle l'Éternel : Que le sage ne se glorifie pas de sa sagesse, que le fort ne se glorifie pas de sa force, que le riche ne se glorifie pas de sa richesse. Mais que celui qui veut se glorifier se glorifie d'avoir de l'intelligence et de me connaître, de savoir que je suis l'Éternel (Jérémie 9.23,24). Le besoin premier de toute créature humaine est de connaître Dieu de manière spirituelle et salvatrice.

Le point de départ de toute vraie connaissance de Dieu doit être une claire compréhension de ses perfections telles que l'Écriture Sainte les révèle. Comment pourrions-nous faire confiance à un Dieu inconnu, le servir et l'adorer ? Ce livre est l'expression d'un effort pour exposer quelques-unes des principales perfections qui sont en Dieu. Pour tirer un réel profit des pages ci-dessous, que le lecteur supplie Dieu de tout son cœur, en termes précis, de bénir sa lecture et d'appliquer ces vérités à sa conscience et à son coeur pour que sa vie en soit transformée.

Il ne suffit pas de posséder un savoir théorique sur Dieu. Dieu ne se fait connaître à notre âme que dans la mesure où nous nous abandonnons à lui en nous soumettant à son autorité, en cherchant à aligner chaque détail de notre existence sur ses saints préceptes et ses saints commandements. Connaissons, cherchons à connaître l'Éternel [en marchant dans le chemin de l'obéissance] (Osée 6.3). Si quelqu'un veut faire sa volonté, il connaîtra... (Jean 7.17). Ceux du peuple qui connaîtront leur Dieu agiront avec fermeté (Daniel 11.32).

sourceMetadata.title: Babies
sourceMetadata.description:
This issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster delves into the theology of bearing children from a biblical and Puritan perspective.

Babies are made in God’s image, God’s elect come from babies, and God’s promise of salvation was promised and fulfilled in a baby. “She shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins” (Mat 1:20-21). Babies are important.

Explore this fascinating subject with articles from John Calvin, Martin Luther, Thomas Manton, J. R. Miller, Stephen Charnock, Richard Adams, Arthur Pink, Thomas Jacombe, and Thomas Boston.

articles.title: God's Image and God's Blessing
articles.description: a thoughtful examination of God’s creation of man in His own image and the majestic beauty of man as male and female. God specifically designed them to produce babies.

articles.title: Be Fruitful and Multiply
articles.description: an exposition of God’s commandment for human procreation and His great blessing upon it.

articles.title: The Heritage of the Lord
articles.description: Children are not simply the products of a biological act; each is a blessing and gift from God.

articles.title: Loving and Caring for Babies
articles.description: Once God blesses a husband and wife with a baby, what do they do next? This is an encouraging overview of parental responsibilities to God-given little ones.

articles.title: Saved in Childbearing
articles.description: What did Paul mean by women being “saved in childbearing”? This is a helpful explanation of a hotly debated portion of Scripture.

articles.title: Four Necessary Graces
articles.description: Paul said that childbearing women would be saved if they continue in faith, charity, and holiness with sobriety; this is a concise survey of these four graces.

articles.title: Sarah Gave Birth by Faith
articles.description: a hearty encouragement to childbearing women to trust God in the challenges of pregnancy.

articles.title: The Best Support in Childbearing
articles.description: thoughts for husbands and wives on how to face the trials of pregnancy and birthing.

articles.title: When God Withholds Babies
articles.description: God, Who commanded, “Be fruitful, and multiply,” does not open some wombs. How should Christians respond to this heartache?

articles.title: A Child Is Born
articles.description: Thousands of millions of babies have been born since Eve gave birth to history’s first children. But one baby was and is more important than all the rest.

children.title: Bebés
children.description: Esta edición de Portavoz de la Gracia se trata de bebés. Juan Calvino presenta este tema vital explicando la majestuosidad creada de hombres y mujeres, y destaca con cuidado que Dios diseñó nuestros cuerpos para engendrar y tener hijos. Martín Lutero nos recuerda que Dios mandó a hombres y mujeres que dieran fruto y se multiplicaran. El puritano Thomas Manton declara con aplomo que los hijos son herencia y recompensa del Señor. Una vez que Dios nos bendice con hijos, ¿qué hacemos con ellos? Para responder a esta pregunta J. R. Miller presenta un resumen maravilloso de cómo amar y cuidar a nuestros bebés. ¿Qué quiso decir Pablo cuando escribió que la mujer “se salvará engendrando hijos”? Stephen Charnock, otro predicador y teólogo puritano, nos da una buena respuesta a esta pregunta difícil. Richard Adams, también predicador puritano, nos ofrece una perspectiva general de las cuatro gracias necesarias para tener hijos y nos ofrece un segundo artículo acerca de la mejor manera de animar y apoyar a la mujer embarazada. A. W. Pink explica la gran fe de Sara de que concebiría en su vejez. El puritano Thomas Jacombe ofrece consuelo a aquellos que no pueden tener hijos. Y, por último, Thomas Boston enfoca el tema del bebé más importante de todos los tiempos.

children.description: Ofrecemos este número del Portavoz de la Gracia: "Rebeldía". Varios expertos “médicos del alma”, examinan y diagnostican esta enfermedad espiritual. En su primer artículo, Andrew Fuller nos ayuda a reflexionar sobre la naturaleza y los síntomas de la enfermedad de la rebeldía. Más adelante, muestra los efectos perjudiciales que esta enfermedad del alma produce en nuestras vidas. William S. Plumer nos guía a través de un examen minucioso de los pasos que conducen a esta condición maligna. Con gran habilidad, Octavius Winslow nos ayuda a reconocer cómo nuestro amor por Cristo puede estar decayendo. En su segundo artículo, prescribe una terapia bíblica para recuperarse de esta dolencia. Joel R. Beeke demuestra que iglesias enteras pueden sufrir esta plaga. Por último, mostrando una actitud tierna y comprensiva, Charles Spurgeon ministra palabras de sanación y recuperación para los que se han rebelado.

sourceMetadata.title: Baptism: A Burial
sourceMetadata.description: Spurgeon addresses the precious symbolism of baptism for the believer. He shows that baptism is for true followers of Christ, who desire to be publicly associated with Him. Jesus, as the substitute for His people, suffered and died, presenting the only acceptable sacrifice to God the Father for the believer’s sins. Baptism shows the believer’s acceptance that Christ’s sacrifice is for the believer himself. He admits that he deserved the death Christ died for him. The believer, buried with Christ in baptism, looks forward to resurrection with Him, after which he walks in “newness of life,” no longer answering to the dominion of sin. Having been where Christ went, the believer desires to go where Christ goes. “Because I live, ye shall live also.”

children.title: El bautismo: una sepultura
children.description: Spurgeon aborda el precioso simbolismo del bautismo para el creyente. Muestra que el bautismo es para los verdaderos seguidores de Cristo, quienes desean identificarse públicamente con Él. Jesús, como sustituto de su pueblo, sufrió y murió, ofreciendo a Dios Padre el único sacrificio aceptable por los pecados del creyente. El bautismo manifiesta que el creyente acepta que el sacrificio de Cristo fue hecho por él mismo; reconoce que merecía la muerte que Cristo sufrió en su lugar. El creyente, sepultado con Cristo en el bautismo, aguarda la resurrección junto a Él, tras lo cual camina en «novedad de vida», sin estar ya sujeto al dominio del pecado. Habiendo estado donde Cristo estuvo, el creyente desea ir adonde Cristo va. «Porque yo vivo, vosotros también viviréis».

files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Baptismal Regeneration
sourceMetadata.description: Spurgeon addresses the idea of baptismal regeneration. “He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.” Believing faith is of primary importance, and baptism is secondary to it. Baptism is an outward act of obedience, a public testimony to the work of grace that has been completed inwardly. One may be baptized, and yet be damned to hell because he did not believe in faith and repent of sin. Spurgeon discusses the deceitfulness of many aspects of infant baptism, which some say imparts regeneration upon the recipient by mere ceremony, with or without the gift of faith.

children.title: Regeneración bautismal, La
children.description: Spurgeon aborda la idea de la regeneración bautismal. «El que crea y sea bautizado será salvo; pero el que no crea será condenado». La fe que cree es de importancia primordial, y el bautismo es secundario a ella. El bautismo es un acto externo de obediencia, un testimonio público de la obra de gracia que se ha consumado interiormente. Uno puede ser bautizado y, sin embargo, ser condenado al infierno por no haber creído con fe ni haberse arrepentido del pecado. Spurgeon analiza el carácter engañoso de muchos aspectos del bautismo infantil, el cual, según algunos, confiere la regeneración al receptor mediante la mera ceremonia, con o sin el don de la fe.

A pesar de haber gozado de gran belleza y una crianza privilegiada, pero habiendo caído en lo más profundo de la vergüenza, la rebeldía y la desesperación, escribió este poema utilizando la belleza y el simbolismo de la nieve para ilustrar su propia vida. sourceMetadata.title: Beginning at Jerusalem
sourceMetadata.description: Christ taught His disciples what He would have them preach: repentance and remission of sins. Spurgeon teaches that repentance is leaving that which was once loved, forsaking it forever. Sin cannot be pardoned if the sinner still loves it. Repentance is the commandment of God. The second theme Christ taught the disciples to preach was remission of sins. God voluntarily forgives of His own grace. Remission of sins is final and irreversible; once sins are pardoned, they are gone forever. The offering of Christ on the cross has put away all guilt of every believer. Christ told how and where to preach: in His name, on His authority, beginning at Jerusalem where these things had come to pass. Spurgeon exhorts that the gospel should always be taught first at home. What kind of testimony is it if the believer witnesses to everyone, but his own children are rebellious and stubborn unbelievers? God’s grace must begin at home, in our own churches and communities, before it can be spread around the world.

sourceMetadata.title: Benefits of Christ, The
sourceMetadata.description:
The Benefits of Christ was arguably the most popular book of the short lived Italian Reformation. It is estimated that 40,000 to 80,000 copies were printed between 1541-1548, of which very few remain today due to the fact that most were burned once the title was placed on the list of prohibited books during the Inquisition. The treatise was originally published anonymously under the title Trattato Ultilissimo Del Beneficio Di Geisu Christo Crocifisso, and was for a few hundred years mistakenly attributed to Aonio Paleario (1503-1570), a martyr for the Reformation cause in Italy. But most scholars now agree, based on records from the Inquisition itself, that the “Trattato” was written by Don Benedetto, a student of the Spanish Reformer Juan de Valdes (1498?-1541) and friend of Peter Martyr Vermigli (1499- 1562). 

The subjects of this booklet include original sin, the purpose of the Law, our salvation depends upon Christ, the effects of living faith, clothed with Christ, and remedies against unbelief.

sourceMetadata.title: Bethlehem and Its Good News
sourceMetadata.description:
"There was nothing great about Bethlehem.  It was 'little among the thousands of Judah' (Mic 5:2); perhaps but a shepherd-village or small market-town; yet there the great purpose of God became a fact; 'The Word was made flesh.'"

Thus begins this tract by Horatius Bonar about the incarnation.  Here we see the glory of God becoming man and the love that God showed in sending His Son to live and die in humility.  At Bethlehem we can learn about the way to God, the vanity of the earth, a life of holiness, a heart of humility, and self denial.

children.title: Belén y las buenas nuevas
children.description:
“Belén no tenía nada de grandioso. Era pequeña para ser en los millares de Judá (Mi. 5:2); quizá apenas una aldea de pastores o un pueblo cuya vida giraba alrededor del mercado; no obstante, allí el gran propósito de Dios se convirtió en un hecho. El Verbo fue hecho carne”.
Así comienza este tratado de Horatius Bonar sobre la encarnación. Aquí vemos la gloria de Dios haciéndose hombre y el amor que Dios mostró al enviar a Su Hijo a vivir y morir en humildad. En Belén podemos aprender sobre el camino a Dios, la vanidad de la tierra, una vida de santidad, un corazón de humildad y negación propia.

sourceMetadata.title: Bible, The
sourceMetadata.description:
Who authored the Bible? What is its power? How should we read it?

Spurgeon answers these and more questions in this insightful booklet taken from three of his sermons on the Book of books.

In the second section, after explaining the power of God's Word, he exhorts us, "Brothers and sisters, let us greatly reverence the Word of God.  If it be all this, let us read it, study it, prize it, and make it the man of our right hand.  And you that are not converted, I do pray you treat the Bible with a holy love and reverence, and read it with the view of finding Christ and His salvation in it."

sourceMetadata.title: Biblical Elders and Deacons
sourceMetadata.description: Christ's will as revealed in Scripture is the pattern for the church, and Nehemiah Coxe unfolds aspects of that pattern that relate to church leadership. "The edification and beauty of the Church is much concerned in her order, not such an order as superstition will dictate, or litigious nicety contend for, but such as sets her in a conformity with Christ's will; and particularly the filling up of the offices which He has appointed, with persons duly qualified for the administration of them, and the regular acting both of officers and members in their respective positions."

sourceMetadata.title: Biblical Parenthood
sourceMetadata.description: What are the duties of Christian parents to their children? More importantly, what are Christian parents' responsibilities to the God who gave them that vital role of shepherding their little ones to the Kingdom of God? This issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster on parenting addresses these vital questions with articles from time-proven pastors such as the Puritans, Martyn Lloyd-Jones, J. C. Ryle. Topics include discipline, training, obstacles, character, and the family's relationship to the world around.

articles.title: Art of Balanced Discipline, The
articles.description: It is easy and common for parents to be imbalanced in disciplining their children; this is an excellent corrective.

articles.title: Bringing Up Children for God
articles.description: a reminder that our children belong to God and that we must bring them up for Him.

articles.title: Calamity of Ungodly Children, The
articles.description: Experience reveals that even the best, most conscientious parents can have ungodly children.

articles.title: Directions for Grieving over Ungodly Children
articles.description: Whether parents are aware of it or not, there are ways of grieving that honor Christ and there are sinful ways of grieving as well.

articles.title: Nurture and Admonition
articles.description: an exposition of what it means to bring up children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

articles.title: Primary Obligations of Parents
articles.description: a detailed list and discussion of parental obligations for bringing up children for God.

articles.title: Principle Obstacles in Bringing Up Children for Christ
articles.description: Parents find many difficulties in their efforts to bring up their children according to God’s Word. Here is a list of common obstacles.

articles.title: Teaching Children about God
articles.description: a helpful explanation of what parents should teach their children about God, His character, and His saving work in His only begotten Son Jesus Christ.

articles.title: Teaching Children Character
articles.description: a useful and insightful guide for instilling good character in our children.

articles.title: Unique Opportunity of Witnessing to the World, A
articles.description: If parents are faithful in bringing up children for Jesus Christ, godly family life becomes a wonderful testimony of Christ’s saving grace.

children.title: Formación bíblica de los hijos en el hogar
children.description: ¿Cuáles son los deberes de los padres cristianos hacia sus hijos? Y, lo que es aún más importante: ¿cuáles son las responsabilidades de los padres cristianos ante el Dios que les ha encomendado esa función vital de guiar a sus pequeños hacia el Reino de Dios? Esta edición del Portavoz de la Gracia, dedicada a la crianza de los hijos, aborda estas cuestiones fundamentales mediante artículos de pastores de probada trayectoria, tales como los puritanos, Martyn Lloyd-Jones y J. C. Ryle. Entre los temas tratados se incluyen la disciplina, la formación, los obstáculos, el carácter y la relación de la familia con el mundo que la rodea.

sourceMetadata.title: Biblical Repentance: Need of the Hour
sourceMetadata.description: "Why is Biblical repentance the need of this hour? Because we are living in a day when most religious leaders actually deny the need for repentance."  Thus Pastor Shelton opens this booklet on the nature and necessity of true repentance.  First, he presents the underlying problem of man's sin which calls for repentance.  Second, he defines and explains what repentance is and how it is connected with faith.  Third, he brings us to the means of repentance, which is the Word of God. Last, he shows us the fruits of genuine repentance in a hatred for sin and a desire for holiness.

articles.title: The Connection of Repentance and Faith

children.title: Arrepentimiento bíblico
children.description: "¿Por qué es el arrepentimiento bíblico la necesidad de esta hora? Porque vivimos en una época en que la mayoría de los líderes religiosos realmente niegan la necesidad de arrepentimiento". Por lo tanto, el pastor Shelton explica en este folleto la naturaleza y la necesidad del verdadero arrepentimiento. Presenta el problema subyacente del pecado del hombre que hace que el arrepentimiento sea necesario, define qué es el arrepentimiento y explica cómo está conectado con la fe. En tercer lugar, nos lleva a los medios del arrepentimiento, que es la Palabra de Dios. Por último, nos muestra los frutos del arrepentimiento genuino en un odio por el pecado y un deseo de santidad.

sourceMetadata.title: Birth of Christ, The
sourceMetadata.description: Here Spurgeon preaches a sermon on Isaiah 7:14-15. "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good." He shows us the glorious miracle of Christ's birth to a lowly virgin.  He explains how the food that Christ ate show us his humanity and his wisdom.  Last we see the glory of the meaning of the name Immanuel.

Comerá mantequilla y miel, hasta que sepa desechar lo malo y escoger lo bueno". Él nos muestra el glorioso milagro del nacimiento de Cristo a traves una humilde virgen. Explica cómo la comida que Cristo comió nos muestra su humanidad y su sabiduría. Por último vemos la gloria del significado del nombre Emanuel.

sourceMetadata.title: Blood of Jesus, The
sourceMetadata.description:
The blood of Christ is here shown to be crucial to all the blessings of our salvation, including our forgiveness, peace, joy, holiness, and regeneration. Reid spends twelve chapters speaking of the glory of the atonement through Christ's blood and its effects in our lives.

"We believe that the refreshing truth, that 'the blood of Jesus Christ, his Son, cleanseth us from all sin' (1Jo 1:7), is the great central sun that sheds a flood of light on the whole system of divine revelation. Atonement by the blood-shedding of Christ is the substratum of Christianity, for the sole ground of a sinner's peace with God is 'the blood of Jesus.'"            —from Chapter 11.

sourceMetadata.title: Blood of the Covenant, The
sourceMetadata.description:
Scripture abounds with references to the blood, the first being “Thou shalt bruise His heel.” This bruised heel of the woman’s seed refers to the foundation of our deliverance. Death was the penalty of man’s sin. If another life be taken for us, and another death replace ours, that blood is taken from the victim and transferred to us. This is the substitutionary death that Jesus died on our behalf. Bonar examines many aspects of how the blood of the Sacrifice is presented in Scripture, the many blessings connected with it, and the ways in which we come into contact with it.

Refresh your soul with this delightful portrayal of all the blessings that flow from the work of Christ.

sourceMetadata.title: Bondage of the Will, The
sourceMetadata.description: The Bondage of the Will is considered by many to be Luther’s most important book, and it stands today as one of the great classics in Christian history. He wrote in 1525 at the beginning of the Reformation in answer to a work by Erasmus, the classical scholar and humanist (1469-1536). Both Erasmus and Luther rejected many of the erroneous practices of the Roman Catholic church. But Luther went further to challenge the Roman teaching of salvation by works. Erasmus pleased the Pope by writing to uphold the Roman dogma of “free will,” that man could of himself decide to choose for his salvation. Luther saw correctly that the Biblical doctrines of the depravity of man and salvation by faith alone stand together. He declared Erasmus to be an enemy of the faith, and wrote The Bondage of the Will to establish this doctrine at the core of evangelicalism. The Modern English Series are modernized abridgments of great Christian classics, for a blessing to many worldwide.

children.title: La esclavitud de la voluntad  (condensado)
children.description: La esclavitud de la voluntad es el libro considerado por muchos como el más importante de Lutero, y se cuenta entre uno de los grandes clásicos de la historia cristiana. Lo escribió en 1525, al principio de la Reforma como respuesta a una obra de Erasmo, el erudito y humanista clásico (c.1466-1536). Tanto Erasmo como Lutero rechazaban muchas de las prácticas erróneas de la Iglesia Católica Romana. Pero Lutero fue más allá, al punto de desafiar la enseñanza romana de la salvación por obras. Lutero vio correctamente que las doctrinas bíblicas de la depravación del hombre y la salvación sólo por fe permanecen juntas. Declaró que Erasmo era un enemigo de la fe, y escribió La esclavitud de la voluntad para establecer esta doctrina como el núcleo del evangelismo.

sourceMetadata.title: Boys and Girls Playing
sourceMetadata.description: Boys and Girls Playing describes God's concern for children in winsome terms easy for a child to understand. Drawing from the fact that in the restored Jerusalem "the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing" (Zec 8:5), Ryle assures little ones that God thinks about boys and girls and He allows them to play. Then he urges them in their playing to remember the eye and ear of God, keep their tempers, not neglect work because of play, and to remember that true happiness comes not from the innocent joys of play but from Christ alone.

children.title: Muchachos y muchachas que jugarán
children.description: Muchachos y muchachas que jugarán describe el cuidado de Dios por los niños en términos atractivos y fáciles de entender para un niño. Partiendo del hecho de que en la Jerusalén restaurada “las calles de la ciudad estarán llenas de muchachos y muchachas que jugarán” (Zacarías 8:5), Ryle asegura a los pequeños que Dios piensa en los niños y las niñas y les permite jugar. Luego, les insta a que recuerden los ojos y los oídos de Dios, mantengan su temperamento, no descuiden el trabajo debido al juego y recuerden que la verdadera felicidad no proviene de los placeres inocentes del juego, sino solo de Cristo.

files.title: Richard Baxter on Worship & Catholicity against Separatism & John Owen
files.author: Richard Baxter, Travis Fentiman, John Owen
files.subjects: Richard Baxter; John Owen; Ecclesiology; Worship; Reformed Worship; Separatism; English Puritanism; Puritan Worship; English Nonconformists; English Nonconformity; Congregationalism; Church; Anglican Church; Anglican Liturgy; Anglican Prayer-Book
files.licence: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/

sourceMetadata.creator: Richard Baxter, Travis Fentiman, John Owen
sourceMetadata.description:
Separatism is often heralded as the height of Christian virtue, that one must separate from nearly every church or worship error. Many Christians who would not go that far, may yet have latent separatistic tendencies. Richard Baxter, in this newly cleaned up piece, demolishes the principles of Separatism. 

His opponent? John Owen. Owen had written a tract arguing for separation, at least for those who had “engaged unto reformation,” from ever attending the Anglican liturgy. In it Owen uses principles that may sound like the height of righteousness, but are separatist. Baxter (rightly) convicts him of 42 errors. 

The article has an editor’s Introduction. If you have interest in worship issues, you will learn a lot. May it humble us and cause us to more greatly love the Lord, his worship and his people.

sourceMetadata.description: Thomas Brooks contrasts the true Christian with the deceitful hypocrite. As he considers the dark state of the hypocrite against the sincere light of the truth of God in the Christian, he reminds the reader: "The ends of a man’s actions are always a great discovery either of sincerity or hypocrisy." After exploring the sinfulness of hypocrisy and the blessedness of God-glorifying sincerity, Brooks gives remedies to the spirit of hypocrisy and principles to aid the soul which "sets the crown on  Christ’s head alone; he will set  God upon the throne, and make all  things else his servants, or his footstool. . . The daily language of sincere souls is this:  Not unto us, Lord,  not unto us,  Lord, but  to thy  name be all the glory."

sourceMetadata.description: A Call to Prayer was one of J.C. Ryle’s best received works in his day and has remained so ever since. sourceMetadata.title: Candid Examination of the Scofield Bible, A
sourceMetadata.description:
“The Scofield Bible may be called perhaps the most influential single work thrust into the religious life of America during the twentieth century. Those who use this work are, in other respects, among the best Christians in our churches. These good people do not lack faith and zeal, but they sadly lack knowledge; and the tragedy of the situation lies just here, that this is the very thing they think they have obtained from the Scofield Bible! In general Bible knowledge, Scofield makes many mistakes, and in his eschatology he goes far astray from anything the Church has ever believed.”

This booklet holds four erroneous doctrinal areas of the Scofield Bible up to biblical light to reveal its errors and set the reader on the right path of orthodox Christianity: 1) artificial typology, 2) doctrine of dispensations and covenants, 3) eschatology, and 4) doctrine of the church.

files.author: Chapel Library contributors
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Canons of Dort, The
sourceMetadata.description:
The Canons of Dort is the explanation of the judicial decision regarding objections to the faith of the Reformation, from the official church council held in The Netherlands in 1618-1619. Jacobus Arminius (1560-1609) was a Dutch theologian and prominent pastor in Amsterdam. He was eloquent and well educated, his sermons attracting large audiences not only for their content but for their controversy. According to Arminius, the orthodox faith of the Reformation was wrong. He taught that God chooses for salvation only those whom He has foreseen will believe. By 1592 Arminius had been formally accused of heresy. In 1610, his zealous followers presented five objections to the standard confessions of faith from the Reformation; the theology behind these objections came to be called Arminianism.

The whole church was caught up with theological debate, and a council was called to resolve the controversy. The Synod of Dort concluded with a rejection of Arminianism, and in The Canons of Dort set forth the orthodox Reformed doctrine on each point; today these are sometimes referred to as the doctrines of grace. As termed in the original preface, it is a “judgment, in which both the true view agreeing with God’s Word concerning the aforesaid five points of doctrine is explained, and the false view disagreeing with God’s Word is rejected.”

files.author: Erroll Hulse
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Catechism for Boys and Girls, A
sourceMetadata.description:
This simple catechism is very helpful for teaching young children to understand and remember the basic truths of the Christian faith.

The Westminster Assembly produced not only its well-known Confession of Faith, but also the Longer Catechism (for pastors’ use in teaching their congregations) and Shorter Catechism (for parents’ use in teaching their children). Soon thereafter, Benjamin Keach (1640-1704) tailored the Westminster Shorter Catechism to the London Baptist Confession of 1677/89 (which is based on the Westminster except in its chapters on church government, the covenants, and baptism). Later, Charles Spurgeon (1834-1892) updated Keach’s catechism for his own congregation.

More recently, Erroll Hulse knew that a more simplified Baptist catechism was needed so that parents could train their young children at home. The 134 short questions and answers encompass all the key doctrines of the faith, including sections on God-Man-Sin, Salvation, The Ten Commandments, Prayer, The Word, The Church and Ordinances, and Last Things.

children.description:
作者介绍

埃罗·胡尔斯 (Erroll Hulse, 1931 - 2017) 从 1970 年到 2014 年在英国里兹 (Leeds, England) 的里兹改革宗浸信会教堂担任副牧师。他编辑并大量广泛地为一本每两个月出刊的国际杂志 (Reformation Today)，撰写了许多书籍和文章包括各种各样的教义、 历史、和实用性，注释的文章，以及世界各地的新闻。

胡尔斯牧师研究神学是在伦敦圣经学院 (London Bible College) 的校长 E F Kevan指导下研读；在伦敦期间，他从钟马田 (Martyn Lloyd-Jones) 的事工中受益。他在英国的库克菲尔德、西苏塞克斯 (Cuckfield West Sussex) 做牧师 23 年，在利物浦(Liverpool) 做三年，在里兹改革宗浸信会的教堂做了十九年的副牧师。

children.title: Gatigisimu y’Abahungu n’Abakobwa
children.description:
Mu Rwanda usanga hari ibitabo bike (imfashanyigisho) biri mu Kinyarwanda byigisha inyigisho nzima, ahubwo ugasanga ibyinshi byigisha ibintu mu buryo budahura n’ukuri kw’ibyanditswe byera, bigatuma abantu benshi batamenya ukuri ahubwo bagakomeza kwizera ibyo babasha gusoma mu rurimi bumva (Ikinyarwanda). Ikindi usanga abantu babasha kubona ibitabo bizima biba biri mu ndimi z’amahanga, abatabasha kuzumva bikaba ari ikibazo kuri bo.

Gatigisimu ni agatabo k’ibibazo n’ibisubizo ku bintu by’ibanze abakristo bizera. Aka gatabo umuntu wese yakwiga ibirimo kugira ngo asobanukirwe ubutumwa bwiza, by’umwihariko wagakoresha wigisha abana kandi bakaba basobanukirwa neza ijambo ry’Imana mu buryo bworoshye kandi bwumvikana. Iyi Gatigisimu yigisha ubutumwa bwiza ubwizera wese yaba umukuru cyangwa umuto arakizwa.

Ku bantu bigisha abana bato haba mu ngo cyangwa n’ahandi hantu hose bigishirizwa ijambo ry’Imana nabasaba rwose gukoresha iyi gatigisimu, kugira ngo ubafashe kwiga neza ijambo ry’Imana, ntekereza ko bibaye byiza mwajya mukora ibibazo bike bishoboka icy’ingenzi ni uko bumva kuruta uko mwakwihutira kuyisoza, mushobora kuyikora mu gihe cy’umwaka (ku bana).

Mu gihe waba wigisha abana ni byiza ko bafata mu mutwe ibyo biga ndetse mugasoma n’ibyanditswe kuri buri kibazo mugezeho.

‘‘Kandi uzi yuko uhereye mu buto bwawe wamenyaga ibyanditswe byera bibasha kukumenyesha ubwenge, bwo kukuzanira agakiza gaheshwa no kwizera Kristo Yesu (2 Timoteyo 3:15)’’.

files.title: Children Brought to Christ, Not to the Font
files.author: Charles H. Spurgeon
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Children Brought to Christ, Not to the Font
sourceMetadata.description:
Charles Spurgeon preached this sermon, based on Mark 10:13-16, in response to “replies” he received upon his sermon titled Baptismal Regeneration. His Anglican detractors used this text to try to show that keeping infants away from the baptismal font was equal to keeping them away from Christ and out of the Kingdom of Heaven. Thus, they said, Spurgeon was incurring the wrath of God on himself by preaching against baptismal regeneration.

Spurgeon shows that Mark 10:13-16 has no connection with baptism. The parents who brought their children to Christ in these verses, did not bring them to Him to be baptized, but that He should touch them, and as Matthew’s gospel says, pray over them. Spurgeon examines this portion carefully, giving many reasons why baptism is not implied by this passage. Christ’s displeasure was directed toward the disciples for discouraging those who come to Him themselves, as well as those who would bring others to Him. Prayers and teaching for the conversion of souls are always pleasing to God. Spurgeon encourages every believer to labor for the salvation of souls, but not through false hopes as some Anglicans teach with their doctrine of infant baptism and baptismal regeneration.

files.title: Children To Be Educated for Christ
files.author: Edward W. Hooker
files.licence: Publisher freely offered electronic edition for personal use; source notices retained
files.contributor: Chapel Library / Mount Zion Bible Church

sourceMetadata.title: Children To Be Educated for Christ
sourceMetadata.description: An instructive message by Edward Hooker for thoughtful Christian parents who desire to raise their children to be useful servants of Christ. Parents, as well as Christian ministers and teachers, need to teach the children in their charge not only love for God and His work, but must also teach them that their will must be secondary to the work of Christ’s kingdom. This is best done by setting a good example in every aspect of life, first, by prayer, then by faithful teaching, and instilling in them early the need for conversion in preparation for a life of service and love for God alone. Christian mothers are a special blessing to the world, having and being in the best position to constantly influence and guide their children in this way.

children.title: Eduque a los niños para Cristo
children.description: Un mensaje instructivo de Edward Hooker dirigido a padres cristianos reflexivos que desean criar a sus hijos para que sean siervos útiles de Cristo. Tanto los padres como los ministros y maestros cristianos deben enseñar a los niños a su cargo no solo a amar a Dios y a su obra, sino también a subordinar su propia voluntad a los intereses del reino de Cristo. La mejor manera de lograrlo es dando un buen ejemplo en todos los aspectos de la vida: primero mediante la oración y luego a través de una enseñanza fiel, inculcándoles desde temprana edad la necesidad de la conversión como preparación para una vida de servicio y de amor exclusivo hacia Dios. Las madres cristianas constituyen una bendición especial para el mundo, ya que se encuentran en la posición ideal para influir y guiar constantemente a sus hijos en este sentido.

Bonar demuestra que, a pesar de este conflicto del hombre contra Dios, Dios ha provisto esperanza —un camino hacia la reconciliación— a través del Hijo de Dios crucificado.

children.title: Christ est mort pour des impies
children.description: Ce tract d'évangélisation montre que Dieu témoigne contre l'homme, révélant qu'il est pécheur. Par nature, l'homme est en état d'inimitié constante envers Dieu. Le plus grand de tous les péchés est que l'homme ne croit pas au nom du Christ et ne l'aime pas. Bonar démontre que, malgré ce conflit de l'homme contre Dieu, ce dernier a offert un espoir — une voie de réconciliation — par le Fils de Dieu crucifié.

Shelton reminds us that all things are Christ's, as Creator and Savior, and all will bow to His sovereign rule. The nature of Christ's Lordship over every "phase in the scope of salvation" calls us to bow in submission to His majesty. He ends with this statement: "Dear friend, these things we have spoken of today surely picture our Lord in all His glory as King, Ruler over all. Do you know Him as Lord? Have you bowed at His feet in repentance and faith? Has he come into your heart and subdued you by conquest?"

La naturaleza del Señorío de Cristo sobre cada "fase en el alcance de la salvación" nos llama a someternos en sumisión a Su majestad. Termina con esta declaración: "Querido amigo, estas cosas de las que hemos hablado hoy seguramente representan a nuestro Señor en toda Su gloria como Rey Gobernante sobre todo. ¿Lo conoces como Señor? ¿Te has inclinado a Sus pies en arrepentimiento y fe? ¿Ha venido a tu corazón y te ha sometido al conquistarte?

In Christ, "Is  not  this,  then,  truly  blessed?  To  have  such  complete  provision  made  for  our  pardon  and  acceptance,  as  well as  for  the  acceptance  of  our  holy  things!  To  have  such  an  High  Priest  over  the  house  of  God—that  house  into which  we,  in  believing,  entered,  and  from  which  we  shall  go  out  no  more!  We  are  'complete  in  Him.'  In ourselves  most  incomplete,  in  our  duties  most  incomplete,  in  our  worship  most  incomplete,  but  yet  in  Him COMPLETE!"

sourceMetadata.title: Christ the Mediator
sourceMetadata.description: God is infinite and holy. Man is merely a creature, and a rebellious, sinful creature. What can bring God and man together--the one Mediator Jesus Christ. The office of Christ as Mediator is essential to our salvation as well as to our peace and spiritual comfort. Enjoy these articles on the subject.

articles.title: Christ the Mediator of the New Covenant
articles.description: an introduction to the great theme of Christ’s incarnation and the glory and beauty of His person as the God-man, the one mediator between God and men.

articles.title: Fullness of the Mediator
articles.description: an in-depth survey of the fullness of Christ’s glorious attributes, coupled with the Spirit of grace and the blessings of grace in Christ that give eternal life to unworthy sinners.

articles.title: Mediator of the Covenant Described in His Person, Nature
articles.description: a thorough survey of Christ’s nature and His fitness for the work of redemption, along with a detailed study of His prophetic, priestly, and kingly offices.

articles.title: Mediator, A
articles.description: a challenging exposition of Paul’s difficult passage, Galatians 3:20, plainly explaining our need for a mediator and how Christ perfectly meets that need. It closes with an earnest plea for sinners to believe on the Mediator for the pardon of sins.

articles.title: Of Christ the Mediator
articles.description: Chapter 8 of the Confession that beautifully summarizes in ten paragraphs the person and work of Jesus Christ our Lord and Savior.

articles.title: Of Christ’s Offices in General
articles.description: a helpful survey of Christ’s offices as Prophet, Priest, and King, showing the reality and the necessity of these offices, when He executed them, and how to receive Him as the great and glorious Redeemer.

children.title: Cristo el Mediador
children.description:
La Palabra de Dios declara: “Porque hay un solo Dios, y un solo mediador entre Dios y los hombres, Jesucristo hombre” (1 Ti. 2:15). Todo lo que ha hecho Dios para salvar a su pueblo de sus pecados en la Persona y obra de su Hijo se resume en la palabra mediador. Esta se refiere a las glorias del Cristo que es nuestro Profeta, Sacerdote y Rey. Cristo el Mediador era en un tiempo una expresión común entre el pueblo de Dios y un tema frecuente de sermones y libros entre los pastores.

El puritano Thomas Goodwin escribió un tomo entero sobre el tema. En cambio, esto no sucede en el cristianismo actual. En vista de esto, estoy considerando la posibilidad de dedicar un número entero en los próximos años a cada oficio de Cristo: Profeta, Sacerdote y Rey. ¿Para qué? Para que los hijos de Dios amplíen su comprensión de la gracia y el conocimiento de nuestro Señor. El anhelo de nuestro corazón es que todos nuestros lectores adoren y sirvan a Jesucristo con un fervor siempre creciente al disfrutar de su Persona y su obra.

De la misma manera, porque tantos predicadores leen el Portavoz, ansiamos ver a una generación nueva de predicadores y maestros que proclamen las glorias de esta gran salvación a través del único Mediador entre Dios y los hombres, Jesucristo hombre. Quiera el Señor, nuestro Dios soberano, usar esto para inspirar a muchos de ustedes a predicar una serie sobre este tema  tan importante.

Abundan tantas obras excelentes del pasado, por lo que decidir qué artículos incluir fue realmente difícil.

Thomas Watson y Thomas Boston aportan excelentes introducciones al tema; Charles Spurgeon predica sobre la importancia vital de un Mediador y, página tras página, John Gill se explaya sobre la plenitud de Cristo el Mediador. De seguro que estos nombres son conocidos para la mayoría de nuestros lectores. En cambio, William Whitaker (1547-1595) puede ser nuevo para algunos. Su extenso sermón es virtualmente un curso de Cristología. Aunque a algunos nos parezca un poco técnico, su mensaje es digno de ser estudiado con cuidado.

Whitaker fue un teólogo famoso en su época, más conocido por su defensa de la Escrituras en su obra A Disputation on Holy Scriptures against the Papists (Una disputa con los papistas sobre las Sagradas Escrituras), especialmente Bellarmine y Stapleton. Según dicen, Bellarmine el jesuita tenía un retrato de Whitaker en su despacho. Cuando le preguntaron el motivo respondió que Whitaker era el hereje más erudito que había leído jamás.

Ce a făcut și face Domnul Isus Hristos prin lucrarea Sa de mijlocire, și de ce este important ca orice creștin să cunoască aceasta?

sourceMetadata.title: Christ the Only Refuge!
sourceMetadata.description:
This tract was written by a prisoner to prisoners. Prisons are evil places, where humans prey on each other to gain some advantage or pleasure. Morrison speaks of the only true place of safety and refuge he found: in Christ. Only Christ can protect the soul from the many and diverse snares and temptations found within a prison. Christ is the refuge, and this refuge can only be found by repentant sinners who see the horror of their sin as God sees it. The sinner must abandon all confidence in his own ability to save, and trust Christ to save him. Where is your refuge?

Irish prisoner Billy Morrison shows how David found his comfort and peace in God's care through Jesus Christ. We should do the same in whatever case we find ourselves. This is the reality of the Christian's faith, that he puts his confidence in God who has promised to care for him by the grace of Christ.

sourceMetadata.description: Christ's substitutionary death on the cross is the central reality of Christianity. This issue of the Free Grace Broadcaster brings together several excellent works on this all-important subject.

articles.title: The Meaning of Christ's Cross
articles.description: The Bible uses several senses for “the cross.” This helpful introduction to the subject of Christ’s cross reveals the subject that Paul loved to preach, to write about, and to live upon all the days of his life. Christ upon the cross is the central truth revealed in Holy Scripture.

articles.title: The Crucifixion of Jesus Christ
articles.description: a detailed account of the horrors of Christ’s crucifixion. In His dreadful suffering, Jesus Christ purchased full and free redemption for sinners.

articles.title: The Glory of the Cross
articles.description: an extended exposition of Paul’s gospel of grace and the reason he gloried in the bloody cross of Jesus Christ. Here is a list of the reasons Paul could not glory in himself and why he found joy, peace, comfort, and strength in the justification that comes by faith alone in Christ crucified.

articles.title: The Passion of Christ
articles.description: an in-depth explanation of Christ’s person and what He accomplished in His suffering and death; this detailed examination considers who Christ was, what He gave, to whom it was given, for whom it was given, the manner of giving, and the effect of Christ’s sacrifice.

articles.title: Our Suffering Substitute

children.title: Cristo en la cruz
children.description:
Ofrecemos este número de Portavoz de la Gracia—Cristo en la Cruz. Una vez más, hemos recurrido a un tomo del pasado, le hemos quitado el polvo, escogido los mejores artículos y agregado material nuevo. Junto con las abundantes notas de pie de página y definiciones teológicas, históricas y biográficas además del trabajo editorial completamente nuevo, este Portavoz nos ofrece exposiciones y artículos que nos presentan a Cristo en la detallada y cruda realidad de la cruz.

J. C. Ryle nos da una introducción al significado de la cruz. El autor alemán F. W. Krummacher comienza con los eventos inmediatamente anteriores a la crucifixión y enseguida hace una descripción conmovedora y profunda de los sufrimientos en cuerpo y alma de Cristo. Es ciertamente este un artículo digno de meditar. El horror de la crucifixión de Cristo revela lo nefasto de nuestro pecado: Cristo en la cruz es el pago por todos nuestros crímenes contra el cielo. S. Duytsch, autor del que no hemos podido encontrar información biográfica, nos da una exposición completa de la razón por la cual el apóstol Pablo se gloriaba en la sangrienta cruz de Cristo. Luego nos remontamos a los 1600s y a Thomas Adams, quien pinta un cuadro vívido y poderoso en una reseña de la pasión de Cristo. Es un cofre de tesoros para el alma que ansía comprender el sacrificio de su Salvador. Por último, Charles Spurgeon expone la doctrina de la sustitución para ofrecer al pueblo de Dios un festín de nutritivo alimento.

Christ-centered hymns are often missing in our man-centered church services today.  We desire to see this collection of Christ-exalting hymns used in churches, family worship, Bible studies, jail ministries, personal devotions, sermon preparation, missions, and in whatever useful ways the Lord Himself may guide His people.

sourceMetadata.description: The world is one of the Christian’s three great enemies, along with the flesh and the devil. According to I. C. Herendeen, the world represents the kingdom of Satan, populated by the unregenerate part of humanity. It is fallen human nature in rebellion against God and acting under the influence of the devil. While we are in the world, we must not be of the world—always aware of God’s command, “Be not conformed to this world” (Rom. 12:2). Not only that, but we should consider ourselves travelers in a foreign land, for this world was never meant to be our home. On the other hand, Herendeen cautions us not to stand aloof from all relationships with unconverted people; our Lord certainly did not. In the end he challenges us, “Persevere in your separation from the world…you will never regret having lived too holy and too separated a life.”
